category: U1 L1 - Natural Rights, Rule of Law, and Limited Government (25 Questions)

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_01_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which statement best defines natural rights?
options: Basic rights people possess because they are human
Benefits granted temporarily by an official
Rules that apply only during elections
Powers reserved only to judges
questions.rationale: Natural rights belong to people by virtue of being human; government does not create them.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_02_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which example best illustrates consent of the governed?
options: A ruler inherits permanent authority
Citizens authorize representatives through constitutional elections
An official ignores election results
A military leader suspends all law
questions.rationale: Consent means legitimate governmental authority originates with the people and operates through constitutional procedures.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_03_Enhanced
questions.prompt: What distinguishes republicanism from direct rule by a hereditary monarch?
options: Citizens choose representatives who govern under law
Officials inherit office for life
One ruler controls every public decision
Law applies only to ordinary citizens
questions.rationale: Republicanism uses elected representatives and law rather than hereditary political authority.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_04_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which action most clearly violates limited government?
options: A court reviews an official action
A president exercises a power authorized by the Constitution
A governor claims any action is permitted because of election victory
A legislature follows required procedures
questions.rationale: Limited government means officials possess only lawful, constitutionally authorized power.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_05_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which scenario best demonstrates rule of law?
options: A mayor is investigated under the same law that applies to residents
A leader exempts friends from published law
Police punish criticism without legal authority
An official replaces law with personal preference
questions.rationale: Rule of law requires known laws and accountability for officials as well as citizens.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_06_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which behavior is the strongest example of civic virtue?
options: Ignoring reliable evidence before voting
Studying an issue, listening respectfully, and participating lawfully
Demanding benefits while refusing civic duties
Spreading an unverified claim
questions.rationale: Civic virtue involves informed, responsible participation and concern for the common good.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_07_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why are natural rights different from government-granted privileges?
options: Rights are inherent, while privileges depend on lawful policies or qualifications
Privileges are always more important than rights
Government may remove natural rights for any reason
There is no difference
questions.rationale: Natural rights are inherent; a privilege is created or conditioned by law or policy.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_08_Enhanced
questions.prompt: The Declaration says governments derive just powers from consent. What conclusion follows?
options: Legitimate authority comes from the people
Officials create all rights
Election winners receive unlimited power
Every citizen must agree with every law
questions.rationale: The phrase supports consent of the governed, not unlimited power or unanimous agreement.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_09_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes limited government from rule of law?
options: Limited government concerns boundaries on power; rule of law concerns lawful exercise and accountability
They are unrelated ideas
Rule of law gives leaders unlimited power
Limited government applies only to citizens
questions.rationale: The concepts overlap, but one emphasizes the scope of power and the other lawful procedure and accountability.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_10_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A legislature passes a law but exempts its own members. Which principle is most directly violated?
options: Rule of law
Natural geography
Hereditary succession
Direct democracy
questions.rationale: Officials cannot place themselves above laws that govern others.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_11_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Residents elect council members to act under a city charter. Which two principles are most evident?
options: Consent of the governed and republicanism
Arbitrary power and monarchy
Natural geography and privilege
Judicial review and federalism
questions.rationale: Citizens authorize government and act through elected representatives.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_12_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A police chief seizes a critic’s property although no law authorizes it. Which analysis is strongest?
options: It violates limited government and rule of law
It demonstrates civic virtue
It expands natural rights
It proves consent
questions.rationale: The official lacks lawful authority and substitutes personal will for known law.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_13_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why does consent of the governed not mean unanimous agreement with every decision?
options: Consent concerns the source and constitutional exercise of authority
Consent requires silence
Only officials possess political judgment
Elections eliminate constitutional limits
questions.rationale: People may disagree with a policy while government remains authorized through constitutional processes.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_14_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which is the best non-example of legitimate authority?
options: An agency acts within power granted by law
A court follows published procedure
A leader punishes a critic despite no violated law
Voters select representatives
questions.rationale: Punishment based on personal will rather than law is arbitrary, not legitimate.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_15_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Why does civic virtue matter in a republic?
options: Self-government depends partly on informed and responsible citizen participation
It allows officials to ignore law
It eliminates disagreement
It replaces constitutional limits
questions.rationale: Institutions alone cannot sustain self-government when citizens abandon responsibility and evidence.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_16_Enhanced
questions.prompt: An elected official says, “The voters chose me, so I cannot violate constitutional government.” What is the best response?
options: Election supplies consent, but limited government and rule of law still constrain the official
Election victory removes every legal limit
Natural rights belong only to the official
Republicanism requires permanent office
questions.rationale: Consent authorizes office; it does not create unlimited or lawless power.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_17_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which evidence most directly supports natural-rights reasoning?
options: A source states that people possess rights before creating government
A rule grants a parking permit
An official inherits a title
A schedule lists election dates
questions.rationale: Natural-rights theory places inherent rights before government.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_18_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which scenario emphasizes limited government more than rule of law?
options: The Constitution does not grant an official the claimed power
A published law is applied differently to two citizens
A court follows a hearing procedure
A mayor is prosecuted under a known statute
questions.rationale: The central issue is whether the power exists at all, making limited government the strongest answer.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_19_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which scenario emphasizes rule of law more than limited government?
options: An official possesses a lawful power but applies the rule only to political opponents
The Constitution withholds a power entirely
Citizens select representatives
A person claims an inherent right
questions.rationale: The issue is unequal, arbitrary application of a law, which directly concerns rule of law.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_20_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which response uses civic evidence rather than merely naming a term?
options: “Rule of law is violated because the mayor ignored the published procedure that binds all officials.”
“The answer is law because it sounds familiar.”
“Government is always correct.”
“I chose rights without examining the scenario.”
questions.rationale: A rigorous answer names the principle, cites a specific fact, and explains the connection.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_21_Enhanced
questions.prompt: What is arbitrary power?
options: Power exercised according to personal will instead of known law and fair rules
Authority constrained by a constitution
Citizen participation through elections
A court applying due process
questions.rationale: Arbitrary power replaces public rules with an official’s personal preference.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_22_Enhanced
questions.prompt: A citizen uses AI to generate a constitutional claim. What should the student do next?
options: Verify the claim with an official source and write independent reasoning
Submit the AI response unchanged
Assume confident wording proves accuracy
Ask AI to take the graded quiz
questions.rationale: Responsible AI use requires source verification, independent reasoning, and disclosure of meaningful help.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_23_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which response best integrates natural rights and consent?
options: People create government by consent so it can protect rights they already possess
Government creates humanity after an election
Consent permits government to abolish every right
Rights exist only when an official approves them
questions.rationale: Natural-rights and social-contract reasoning place rights first and authorized government second.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_24_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which counterclaim best strengthens an argument that rule of law prevents arbitrary government?
options: Limited government is also necessary because a lawful procedure cannot justify a power government never possessed
Rule of law makes constitutional limits unnecessary
Elections excuse unlawful action
Civic virtue allows selective enforcement
questions.rationale: Strong analysis recognizes that lawful accountability and boundaries on power work together.

questions.name: USG_U01_L01_Quiz_25_Enhanced
questions.prompt: Which conclusion best explains how the six lesson principles work together?
options: Rights belong to people; consent authorizes a republic; constitutional limits and law restrain power; civic virtue supports the system
One election replaces all constitutional principles
Officials create rights and remain above law
Civic participation is unnecessary when laws exist
questions.rationale: The principles form a connected system of rights, legitimate authority, representation, restraints, accountability, and responsibility.
